---
title: "Workflow & data model"
---

## Workflow

Everything from downloading data to rendering this site runs through
[Snakemake](https://snakemake.readthedocs.io) (`Snakefile`, `workflow/rules/`):

* **Python-native, no services.** Rules call the package directly, with no scheduler or
  database to run.
* **A file-based DAG with wildcards.** It maps naturally onto dataset → harmonize → (run ×
  batch) fits → analyses → site.
* **Resumable.** Interrupted runs pick up where they stopped. Each fit job also caches
  per-leaf results, so a killed job restarts at the next leaf.
* **Scalable.** The same rules run on a laptop and on a SLURM cluster. For the full fit, the
  per-batch commands are written out as job files for YCRC's Dead Simple Queue (`docs/hpc.md`).

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph data[Data]
    direction LR
    E[EcoSIS API] --> H
    S[ECOSTRESS library] --> H
    N[NASA SHIFT<br>ORNL DAAC] --> H
    D[spectra_db<br>pinned commit] --> H
    H[harmonize<br>adapters + schema + QC<br>+ species] --> DB[(normalized<br>parquet DB)]
  end
  DB --> SEL[select<br>fit set + batches]
  subgraph fits[Inversions]
    direction LR
    SEL --> F1[stage 1 fits<br>ou error model]
    F1 --> LR[learn<br>Matérn ℓ, discrepancy<br>cross-fitted]
    LR --> F2[stage 2 fits<br>ss / ld error models]
  end
  F1 --> AG[aggregate]
  F2 --> AG
  AG --> AN[analyses<br>A: RTM evaluation<br>B: trait variation]
  AN --> SD[site data<br>release asset]
  SD --> W[this website]
```

**Fit sets** (`config/config.yaml`) select the observations and the runs, where a run is
RTM × error model × R/T correlation × data use:

| Fit set | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `smoke` | A 16-leaf end-to-end test of the whole chain. |
| `pilot` | About 120 observations stratified by dataset, sample state and R+T availability; all error models. |
| `feasibility` | Absorptance and pseudo-absorbance fits. |
| `full` | Every observation, with the configuration chosen in the pilot. |

## Data model

Each source is downloaded by code and converted by a declarative, per-dataset YAML config
(`src/leafrtm/db/adapters/configs/`). The config maps the provider's columns onto one
normalized schema:

```{mermaid}
erDiagram
  DATASET ||--o{ SITE : has
  SITE ||--o{ PLOT : has
  DATASET ||--o{ ENTITY : has
  PLOT ||--o{ ENTITY : located
  SPECIES ||--o{ ENTITY : is
  ENTITY ||--o{ OBSERVATION : "measured at time / state"
  OBSERVATION ||--o{ SPECTRUM : "replicates"
  OBSERVATION ||--o{ TRAIT : "leaf-level"
  ENTITY ||--o{ TRAIT : "pooled / plant-level"
  OBSERVATION }o--o{ TREATMENT : "assigned"
  SPECTRUM }o--|| WAVELENGTH_GRID : "native grid"
  SPECTRUM }o--|| INSTRUMENT : "measured with"
```

* **Entity** is a physical leaf or sample. **Observation** is that entity at one time and in
  one sample state, so the same leaf measured fresh and again after grinding gives one entity
  with two observations. RTMs are inverted per observation.
* **Spectra** keep their native wavelength grid; grids are deduplicated and shared. Values
  are fractions (percent is converted per spectrum).
* **Traits** are converted to canonical units with `pint`. Each carries its trait level (leaf,
  or pooled sample / plant) and measurement method (e.g. optical chlorophyll meters are
  flagged).
* **Enums** cover the categorical metadata:

  | Field | Values |
  |---|---|
  | sample state | fresh, dried intact, pressed, ground |
  | target configuration | single leaf, leaf stack, needle array, single needle |
  | foreoptic | integrating sphere, leaf clip, contact probe, bare fibre |
  | quantity | R, T, A, PA |
  | canopy position, sun/shade, leaf age | fixed levels |
  | treatment factor | nitrogen, water, temperature, CO₂, light, pathogen, herbivory, pollutant, genotype, … |
  | species attributes | growth form, leaf type, phenology, photosynthetic pathway |

## Derived traits and QC

**Derived traits** are added only when not measured, and flagged `derived`:

* EWT $=$ LMA $\cdot W/(1-W)$, with $W$ the water fraction of fresh mass. A previous
  compilation multiplied $W$ by LMA instead.
* N and C per area from per-mass values and LMA.
* Chlorophyll a+b from a and b.

**Physically implausible trait values** are dropped and listed in the harmonization report.

**Spectral QC flags** are recorded, never applied to the values:

* `out_of_range`: more than 5 % of bands outside [−0.02, 1.02]
* `flat`
* `sparse`
* `jump`: a step at a detector join
* `replicate_outlier`: RMS distance from the replicate median

Flagged spectra are excluded from the inversions.

## Species

There are two passes:

1. **Manual review.** Names and USDA codes are matched to the USDA PLANTS checklist. Every
   name not found there is reviewed by hand, and the decisions are committed.
2. **GBIF re-check.** Every resolved name is checked against the GBIF backbone taxonomy
   (accepted name, status, family).

See [Species resolution](species.qmd).
